document.title: Afghanistan: Meeting with the Taliban
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Taliban officials in the US under Unocal auspices meet Assistant Secretary Karl Inderfurth on 8 December 1997. They seek better relations and crop substitution aid, defend gender policies, and pledge to prevent terrorist use of Afghanistan. They say they did not invite Bin Laden, stopped his public interviews, and frustrated Iranian and Iraqi contact attempts.

events.description: Inderfurth and Malinowski met three Taliban acting ministers and Mujahid in Washington.
Malik seized a Taliban negotiating team in Mazar-i-Sharif.
State Department cable reporting the meeting.
Malik's forces seized a Taliban negotiating team in Mazar-i-Sharif.
Reported killing of about 3,000 Taliban prisoners near Mazar.
Inderfurth, Malinowski and Taliban acting ministers (Muttaqi, Ahmad Jan, Din Mohammed, Mujahid) meet in Washington on negotiations, terrorism, bin Laden, pipeline, consular issues.
Muttaqi pledges Taliban will not allow Afghanistan to be used as a base for terrorism.
Taliban hand over non-paper on US friendship, poppy eradication and education aid.
Taliban non-paper presented to U.S. officials, text reported in State cable 231842, listing viewpoints on relations, poppy, education, massacre, Iran/Russia aid, embassy.
Alleged massacre of about 3,000 imprisoned Taliban at Laily Desert near Shibarghan, plus executions in Mazar-i-Sharif and Faryab, per Taliban non-paper.
Iranian flights allegedly deliver arms and ammunition to Bamiyan and Mazar-i-Sharif airports for the opposition.
A/S Inderfurth met three Taliban acting ministers and the UN permrep designate in Washington; Taliban sought improved relations, embassy reopening, drug-crop funding.
State Department cable 97STATE231842 reporting the meeting with the Taliban.
Malik seized a Taliban negotiating team in Mazar-i-Sharif (the North says they were an occupying force).

key_claims: Mullah Omar ordered the Taliban delegation to seek a meeting with the US.
Taliban ministers pledged not to allow Afghanistan to be used as a base for terrorism, citing bin Laden.
Taliban claimed bin Laden was already in Nangarhar as a guest of the previous regime and that they limited his activities.
Din Mohammed warned that expelling bin Laden would send him to Iran.
Taliban alleged Iran and Russia arm the Northern Alliance and that 3,000 Taliban prisoners were massacred.
Taliban sought US aid for crop substitution, an embassy in Kabul and the pipeline, but resisted joining intra-Afghan dialogue.
